votes.question: Booker Amdt. No. 6835 — To establish certain standards with respect to coaches of varsity sports teams.
votes.plain_language: This amendment would have let coaches move between four-year colleges under transfer rules like those for athletes, and it would have voided a coach's endorsement deal unless the pay matched similar non-coaches and had a real business purpose. A Yea would have added those rules. A Nay rejected them.

votes.question: Booker Amdt. No. 6805 — To increase the limitation on funding for post-eligibility insurance and catastrophic injury for student athletes.
votes.plain_language: This amendment would have capped a student-athlete insurance and catastrophic-injury fund at $200 million and required major conferences and an athletic association to cover any amount above $100 million. A Yea would have set that cap. A Nay rejected it.

votes.question: Kennedy Amdt. No. 6760 — To limit price increases for college athletics tickets.
votes.plain_language: This amendment would have barred colleges, conferences, and athletic associations from raising ticket prices for a sport by more than 4 percent from the prior academic year. A Yea would have added that cap. A Nay rejected it.

votes.question: Paul Amdt. No. 6758 — To improve the bill.
votes.plain_language: This amendment would have replaced the college-sports bill with the Collegiate Sports Integrity Act, which centers on an antitrust exemption for athletic conferences and associations. A Yea would have made that swap. A Nay rejected it.

votes.question: Baldwin Amdt. No. 6828 — To modify the provision relating to the relationship of this Act to existing law.
votes.plain_language: This amendment rewrites the college-sports bill's preemption section so states generally cannot set conflicting rules on athlete publicity pay, transfers, or certain eligibility, while keeping state civil-rights, contract, privacy, and similar laws unless they conflict. A Yea adopts that text. A Nay rejects it.

votes.question: H. Con. Res. 89 — A concurrent resolution directing the President, pursuant to section 5(c) of the War Powers Resolution, to remove United States Armed Forces from hostilities with Iran.
votes.plain_language: This House resolution tells the President to remove U.S. forces from hostilities with Iran unless Congress has declared war or authorized that force, while still allowing defense against an imminent attack. A Yea would agree to that direction. A Nay rejects the resolution.

votes.question: Motion to Invoke Cloture: Collins Amdt. No. 6732 to H.R. 6500
votes.result: Cloture Motion Agreed to (91-6, 3/5 majority required)
votes.bill_title: Continuing Appropriations and Extensions Act, 2027
votes.plain_language: This vote would end debate on a substitute that replaces H.R. 6500's Africa-trade text with a stopgap funding the government into fiscal year 2027 and extending several programs. A Yea limits debate on that substitute. A Nay keeps debate open.

votes.question: Motion to Invoke Cloture: Motion to Proceed to H.R. 6500
votes.result: Cloture on the Motion to Proceed Agreed to (89-4, 3/5 majority required)
votes.bill_title: Continuing Appropriations and Extensions Act, 2027
votes.plain_language: This was a vote to end debate on starting consideration of H.R. 6500 as it then stood: an extension of duty-free treatment for certain African imports and of customs user fees. A Yea moves the Senate toward taking up that bill. A Nay blocks ending debate.

votes.question: Motion to Invoke Cloture on the Motion to Proceed: H.R. 7008
votes.result: Cloture on the Motion to Proceed Rejected (53-47, 3/5 majority required)
votes.bill_title: Stop Insider Trading Act
votes.plain_language: This was a vote to end debate on taking up the Stop Insider Trading Act, which would bar members of Congress and their spouses and dependent children from buying stocks and would require public notice before a sale. A Yea would have moved the Senate toward taking up the bill. A Nay blocked ending debate.

votes.question: S. Res. 817
votes.bill_title: An executive resolution authorizing the en bloc consideration in Executive Session of certain nominations on the Executive Calendar.
votes.plain_language: This resolution lets the Senate take up a batch of nominations together instead of one by one, covering executive jobs, judges, ambassadors, and similar posts. A Yea agrees to that group procedure. A Nay does not.

votes.question: Motion to Invoke Cloture: S. Res. 817
votes.bill_title: An executive resolution authorizing the en bloc consideration in Executive Session of certain nominations on the Executive Calendar.
votes.plain_language: This vote would end debate on S.Res. 817, which provides for the en bloc consideration of nominations for various executive officers, judges, ambassadors, and related positions. Cloture needs 60 votes (three-fifths of the Senate). A Yea limits debate so the Senate can move toward a final vote; a Nay keeps debate open.

Cloture needs 60 votes (three-fifths of the Senate). A Yea moves the Senate toward taking up the bill; a Nay keeps debate open.

votes.result: Cloture on the Motion to Proceed Rejected (57-43, 3/5 majority required)
votes.bill_title: Ratepayer Protection Act
votes.plain_language: This was a vote to end debate on taking up a bill that would have state regulators consider making very large power users pay the full extra cost of grid upgrades built to serve them. A Yea would have moved the Senate toward taking up the bill. A Nay blocked ending debate.

votes.question: Motion to Proceed to S. J. Res. 187
votes.bill_title: A joint resolution providing for congressional disapproval under chapter 8 of title 5, United States Code, of the rule submitted by the Environmental Protection Agency relating to "Modification to the Start of the Submission Period for Perfluoroalkyl and Polyfluoroalkyl Substances (PFAS) Reporting and Recordkeeping Under TSCA 8(a)(7)".
votes.plain_language: This was a vote on whether to take up a resolution disapproving an Environmental Protection Agency change to the start date for reporting certain PFAS chemicals. A Yea lets the Senate begin that debate. A Nay blocks taking up the resolution.

votes.bill_title: Digital Asset Market Clarity Act
votes.plain_language: This was a vote to end debate on taking up a bill that would regulate digital commodities through the commodities and securities agencies and restrict a Federal Reserve digital currency offered directly to individuals. A Yea would have moved the Senate toward taking up the bill. A Nay blocked ending debate.

votes.result: Cloture on the Motion to Proceed Rejected (52-46, 3/5 majority required)

votes.plain_language: This was a vote to end debate on taking up a bill that would require photo identification to receive a ballot in a federal election, with a provisional ballot if the voter lacks that ID. A Yea would have moved the Senate toward taking up the bill. A Nay blocked ending debate.

party_line.scope: Senate votes 1–262 of the 119th Congress, session 2 (262 votes, January 5, 2026 to November 12, 2026), from the Senate LIS.

said_voted.caption: Posts are shown as written. A post is matched to a vote only when it names the bill number or the bill's official title. A post can mention a bill for many reasons.
said_voted.topic_caption: Recent posts grouped by simple keyword rules that are identical for every member (published at /x_topic_rules.json). A post listed under a topic is not claimed to be about any specific vote; a post can appear under more than one topic.
said_voted.note: No official X account is listed for this member in the public congress-legislators social-media file, so no posts are shown.

financial_disclosures.caption: Official House financial disclosure filings from the Clerk of the House. A filing lists assets, income, liabilities, and trades the member reported; it is not proof of a conflict or of wrongdoing. Dollar ranges and asset names are in the PDF. This page links to the Clerk's copies and does not score anyone.
financial_disclosures.note: Senate financial disclosures are filed through efd.senate.gov, a different system from the House Clerk index used here. Senate filings are not listed yet.

funding.heading: Disclosed campaign receipts
funding.detail: Federal cards show the principal campaign committee and OpenFEC totals for one two-year cycle, plus itemized Schedule A contributors. House uses 2026. Senate uses the cycle of the next election (2026, 2028, or 2030). This is not career fundraising and does not include Schedule E outside spending. Governors do not get a federal contribution list.

town_halls.note: There is no national town-hall dataset. Dates are not estimated.

disclosure_note: Disclosed contributions only; donors behind groups that do not report their own donors are not in this feed.
vote_scope: This is not a full career record. The cache is the latest 40 House rolls (2026, rolls 275-314) and 40 Senate votes (119th Congress, session 2, votes 217-256).
